**Top of mind:** Google beat Mercor in the bankruptcy auction for Spirit Airlines' internal data — $10M vs Mercor's $7.5M for ~100M emails and 500M chat messages — the clearest sign yet that data vendors are moving from selling labor to buying proprietary corpora outright. Meanwhile the two biggest data buyers keep compounding: Anthropic's run rate hit $65B in July (7x YoY) and Nvidia is backing up to $105B in financing for OpenAI's Ohio buildout.

## Competitor moves

- **Mercor bid $7.5M for Spirit Airlines' corporate data — and lost to Google's $10M (Aug 17).** The bankrupt airline's corpus (~100M emails, 500M Teams messages, 30M lines of code, PII-scrubbed by a third party) went to Google for AI training. Mercor showing up in this auction signals vendors racing to own real enterprise interaction data rather than just produce it — and distressed-company data auctions look like a repeatable sourcing channel worth watching. [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/business-and-practice/google-aims-to-boost-ai-with-purchase-of-spirit-airlines-data), [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/google-wins-spirit-airlines-bankruptcy-data-auction-for-10m)
- **Amazon is industrializing book digitization for AI training (Aug 17).** 404 Media AirTagged a shipment of ~1,000 rare books to Amazon's Las Vegas LAS8 facility, where a dedicated operation cuts off spines and scans pages at scale; Amazon confirmed it buys books "through commercial channels" for product and AI development. Big tech insourcing content acquisition is both competition on the data-sourcing side and fresh copyright/provenance controversy. [404 Media](https://www.404media.co/we-tracked-a-shipment-of-rare-books-it-ended-at-an-amazon-ai-training-facility/)

## New projects & opportunities

- **OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Teens (Aug 18)** — age-prediction routing, quiet hours, blocked self-harm and romantic content, and a study mode, shipped under pressure from teen-safety lawsuits. Every lab will need age-appropriateness policy data, minor-safety red-teaming, and pedagogy-style evals: a new annotation category with regulatory tailwinds. [BNN Bloomberg](https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/business/company-news/2026/08/18/openai-launches-chatgpt-for-teens-promising-a-more-age-appropriate-chatbot/)
- **Unitree's ~$9B Shanghai IPO lists Wednesday after a record 8,000x retail oversubscription (Aug 18).** The first mainland humanoid-robot IPO raised $904M; Unitree shipped ~5,500 humanoids last year at 60% gross margin. A capital-flush humanoid sector means growing demand for teleop demonstrations, manipulation trajectories, and real-world task video — workstreams where India's cost base is competitive. [CNN](https://edition.cnn.com/2026/08/18/tech/china-unitree-ipo-intl-hnk)
- **TELUS Digital is recruiting for a reasoning-annotation project in India at $20–30/hr, remote (live listing).** A current datapoint on frontier-lab demand for India-based reasoning specialists — and on the prevailing rate card for expert work. [The Muse](https://www.themuse.com/jobs/telusdigital/reasoning-annotation-project-opportunity-india)

## Frontier lab movements

- **Anthropic's annualized revenue reached $65B by end of July — up from $47B in May and ~$9B at end-2025 (CNBC, Aug 17).** Disclosed to investors weeks after its confidential IPO filing. One of the two largest buyers of human data is compounding roughly 7x year over year — faster than most vendors' capacity plans assume. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/17/anthropic-says-annualized-revenue-climbed-to-65-billion-in-july.html)
- **Nvidia will guarantee up to $105B in financing for OpenAI's Ohio data center (CNBC, Aug 17).** The SB Energy-built site starts at 4.25GW and can scale to 8GW, with OpenAI as 20-year anchor tenant and first capacity in 2028. Compute commitments of this magnitude lock in years of post-training and evaluation data demand. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/17/nvidia-financing-open-ai-data-center-ohio.html)
- **Baidu's GPU cloud revenue jumped 283% YoY even as overall Q2 sales fell 4% (Aug 18).** AI Cloud Infra grew 50% to RMB 7.3B and AI now represents half of Baidu's general business — Chinese lab and enterprise compute demand keeps accelerating, context for the ongoing debate over US vendors serving Chinese labs. [PR Newswire (Baidu)](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/baidu-announces-second-quarter-2026-results-302853860.html), [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/node/10263)

## Research papers

- **OpenART: Scaling Agent Red Teaming via Open-Ended Environment Evolution** — Yunhao Chen, Xin Wang, Yixu Wang, Yan Teng, Xingjun Ma, Yu-Gang Jiang et al. (arXiv, Aug 1; circulating on Hugging Face's trending list this week). Provides 10,000+ validated stateful scenarios across 50 domains built from a pool of 500K+ tools; its evolutionary attack hits an 85% success rate across 75 agent configurations. Validated agentic environments and safety scenarios at this scale are exactly the dataset category labs are starting to buy — and hand-built, QA'd scenario production is a natural vendor offering. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00677)

## Leadership movements

- Nothing notable today.

**Top of mind:** Scale AI has a permanent CEO again — ex-Illumina chief Francis deSouza took over August 10, signaling a renewed enterprise and government push from the biggest name in the space. Meanwhile Anthropic disclosed ~$11.5B in Q2 revenue (its first profitable quarter) with a fall IPO in preparation, and India's Independence Day address put AI skilling for 10 million youth on the national agenda — lab budgets and India's supply side are both expanding at once.

## Competitor moves

- **Scale AI touts enterprise and government momentum under its new CEO.** Alongside the deSouza appointment, Scale disclosed new enterprise customers BP and Mayo Clinic and expanded business with US and international governments — a signal it is rebuilding its book post-Meta-deal and competing hard for non-lab revenue. [Scale AI](https://scale.com/blog/scale-appoints-new-ceo), [PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/scale-ai-appoints-francis-desouza-as-ceo-to-lead-next-phase-of-companys-growth-302838437.html)
- **Mercor's H1 2026 revenue reported past $614M, ~90% from OpenAI and other frontier labs.** The concentration cuts both ways: expert-network-style human data is scaling fast, but Mercor's dependence on a handful of labs shows how exposed pure-lab suppliers are; it was separately in talks in July to raise ~$500M at a $20B valuation. [BigGo Finance](https://finance.biggo.com/news/865c23cb-3e0d-4c21-aa0d-6bf2a7fc8d1a), [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/richardnieva/2026/07/09/mercor-fundraise/)

## New projects & opportunities

- **India is becoming the hub for physical-AI / robotics training data.** A Bloomberg feature (Aug 12) documents thousands of Indian workers filming everyday manual tasks to train robots for US and Chinese labs, with follow-up reporting citing rates around $2.62/hour — robotics data collection is an open, fast-growing workstream where India-based operators have a structural cost and workforce advantage. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2026-08-12/thousands-of-india-workers-are-helping-ai-firms-train-robots-to-replace-them), [TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/324337/20260813/indian-workers-film-their-own-jobs-262-hour-train-robots-that-will-replace-them.htm)
- **Modi pledges AI training for 10 million Indian youth; Bhashini translates Independence Day speech into 22 languages (Aug 15).** A government-backed AI skilling wave expands the annotator/expert talent pool, and the national showcase of Indic-language AI points to growing demand for Indic-language data pipelines. [TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/324582/20260815/india-deploys-homegrown-ai-red-fort-pledges-ai-training-ten-million-youth.htm)

## Frontier lab movements

- **Anthropic reports ~$11.5B preliminary Q2 revenue — first quarter in the black — as banks prep a fall IPO.** A 14x YoY jump with positive operating income means the best-funded data buyer in the market has more budget headroom, and IPO scrutiny raises the bar on data provenance and quality documentation. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/anthropic-revenue-surges-over-11-210857853.html)
- **The coding/agent benchmark arms race accelerated: Google shipped Gemini 3.7 Flash (Aug 14) with big coding-benchmark jumps; DeepSeek launched V4-Pro the same day.** Both releases compete on coding and agentic benchmarks — sustained demand for high-difficulty coding data, agent trajectories, and evaluation sets. [Google DeepMind](https://deepmind.google/models/model-cards/gemini-3-7-flash/), [Caixin](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-08-14/tech-brief-aug-14-deepseek-launches-v4-pro-and-raises-api-prices-by-as-much-as-1100-102474222.html)
- **Apple trained its own China-specific LLM with Alibaba's help (Reuters, Aug 14) — first foreign company cleared by Beijing to offer a proprietary model in mainland China.** A major new model-training program outside the usual lab set means another serious buyer of localized training and evaluation data. [MacRumors (Reuters report)](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/08/14/apple-trained-own-ai-model-for-china/)
- **Dario Amodei: "the thing that will work is actually curing cancer" (X post, Aug 15).** Anthropic's CEO doubled down on its AI for Science program as the path to rebuilding public trust — a strong signal that demand for expert biology, chemistry, and medical data will keep climbing. [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/08/16/dario-amodei-anthropic-ai-trust-crisis-regulation-frontier-open-models-negative-views/)

## Research papers

- **Scaling Domain Data Repetition in LLM Pretraining — ByteDance Seed.** Studies how many times domain-specific data can be repeated in pretraining before returns collapse; directly informs how much fresh domain data labs need versus recycling, i.e., the economics of domain-data sourcing. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14071), [HF Papers](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.14071)
- **Beyond Final Scores: A Systematic Evaluation of Agents for Long-Horizon AI R&D — Meituan LongCat team.** Argues final-score benchmarks miss how agents fail over long horizons and proposes process-level evaluation — exactly the kind of rubric-driven, human-judged evaluation work data vendors can sell. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13417), [HF Papers](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.13417)
- **PRM-as-a-Judge 1.5: A Toolkit for Robot Process Assessment — 25-author collaboration.** Process reward models for judging robot task execution; pairs with the India robotics-data boom above — vendors who can supply process-annotated robot trajectories are positioned for this wave. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14284), [HF Papers](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.14284)
- **LittleLearner: Language Models Under Pedagogically Controlled Knowledge Exposure — ELLIS Institute Tübingen.** Explores curriculum-style control of what data a model sees during training; strengthens the case for carefully sequenced, curated datasets over bulk collection. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13545), [HF Papers](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.13545)

## Leadership movements

- **Francis deSouza appointed CEO of Scale AI, effective Aug 10.** The former Illumina CEO takes over from interim chief Jason Droege (in place since the June 2025 Meta deal); an operator with public-company and regulated-industry experience suggests Scale is professionalizing for enterprise/government scale — expect sharper competition on compliance-heavy contracts. [Scale AI](https://scale.com/blog/scale-appoints-new-ceo), [PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/scale-ai-appoints-francis-desouza-as-ceo-to-lead-next-phase-of-companys-growth-302838437.html)
- **Google DeepMind reorg: Demis Hassabis steps back to chairman and Alphabet chief scientist; CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu takes day-to-day control; Jeff Dean departs after 27 years to found startup Discovery Loop.** A product-speed-focused DeepMind racing to catch OpenAI and Anthropic (Gemini 3.5 Pro reportedly delayed over coding-benchmark issues) likely means bigger, faster data purchases from Google. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/12/google-deepmind-koray-kavukcuoglu.html), [MarketWatch via MSN](https://www.msn.com/en-us/money/other/a-decade-of-internal-ai-battles-is-finally-catching-up-to-google/ar-AA2ab1gI)

**Top of mind:** Mercor and rival data vendors are now buying the *corpses* of failed startups — internal Slack threads, Jira tickets and workflow recordings — to build reinforcement-learning gyms for OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. This is the clearest signal yet that the money is moving from static annotation to realistic, proprietary enterprise environments, and that "who owns the messy real-world data" beats "who has the biggest labeler bench." Meanwhile Anthropic disclosed $11.5B in Q2 revenue and its first profitable quarter, so the budget on the buy side is only getting bigger.

## Competitor moves

- **Mercor is hunting shuttered startups' Slack and Jira archives for agent training data.** The Information reports Mercor and rivals are licensing internal comms, ticket histories and workflow recordings from companies that are dying or being acquired, turning them into RL gyms where frontier labs train agents on realistic enterprise tasks — Mercor reportedly approached Warmly's CEO after its HubSpot deal. Post-mortem operational data is now a priced commodity, which opens a sourcing lane that has nothing to do with headcount. [The Information](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/startups-find-old-slack-threads-tickets-suddenly-high-demand) · [AI Weekly brief](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/mercor-chases-shuttered-startups-slack-and-jira-archives)
- **Forbes: Surge AI, Mercor and AfterQuery are quietly selling training data to Chinese labs (Aug 5).** Forbes estimates the top six Chinese labs spend ~$500M/year with American data labelers; AfterQuery books $50M+ recurring from Chinese labs while holding a US federal contract, and Tencent buys from Surge, whose US clients include the Army and Air Force. Expect FOCI-style scrutiny, provenance clauses and customer-exclusivity terms to start showing up in every frontier-lab MSA — a compliance burden, but also a wedge for vendors who can prove clean separation. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/annatong/2026/08/05/silicon-valleys-other-china-problem-its-training-their-ai/)
- **Scale AI's Francis deSouza took over as CEO effective Aug 10.** The ex-Google Cloud COO / ex-Illumina CEO replaces interim chief Jason Droege, and Scale is leaning hard into enterprise and government (BP, Mayo Clinic) rather than trying to win back the frontier labs that pulled contracts after Meta's stake. Scale conceding the frontier-lab lane is why Surge owns RLHF and Mercor owns expert marketplaces today. [Scale AI](https://scale.com/blog/scale-appoints-new-ceo) · [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/30/scale-ai-google-cloud-coo-francis-desouza)
- **Appen sets H1 FY26 results for Aug 27.** The only public pure-play in the sector reports in eleven days — the cleanest available read on whether legacy annotation volume is still eroding as spend shifts to expert data and environments. [Appen / ASX](https://kalkine.com.au/news/announcements/appen-to-release-h1-fy26-results-on-27-august-2026)

## New projects & opportunities

- **RL environments are the fastest-growing line item in lab data budgets.** Mercor's July acquisition of Deeptune (a16z-backed, $43M Series A in March) folded computer-use and coding environments into its stack, and The Information reports another RL-gym startup has hit a $750M valuation purely on lab appetite. For an India-based operator this is the highest-margin adjacency available: environment authoring needs domain-expert SMEs and QA, not volume crowds. [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/07/09/ai-unicorn-mercor-acquires-deeptune-brendan-foody-investor-a16z-openai-anthropic/) · [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/07/09/mercor-buys-deeptune-build-training-environments-ai-agents/) · [The Information](https://www.theinformation.com/newsletters/ai-agenda/reinforcement-learning-gym-startup-buoyed-labs-appetite-training-data-reaches-750-million-valuation)
- **Musk told SpaceX staff Grok will be trained on "the sum total of SpaceX information," including their own work.** Fortune reports he framed employees as the AI's "parents"; SpaceX hasn't said what data is in scope or whether staff can opt out. Enterprises copying this playbook will need internal-data curation, consent tracking and de-identification — a services line most labelers don't currently sell. [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/08/14/elon-musk-spacex-employees-grok-ai-training/)
- **UK and Irish secondhand booksellers report mystery bulk orders they believe feed AI training.** One anonymous seller reported orders for 6,000 books since January; Barter Books' Stuart Manley described "masses and masses of AI money being squandered." Physical-corpus acquisition and digitisation is still an unsophisticated, brute-force market — an obvious opening for a vendor offering rights-cleared sourcing plus scanning/OCR at Indian cost structures. [AOL/PA](https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/secondhand-booksellers-uk-ireland-suspect-080051000.html)
- **IndiaAI's AIKosh dataset EOI remains open on a rolling basis.** MeitY is still inviting non-government entities to contribute non-personal, anonymised India-specific datasets and AI artefacts; the platform already hosts 22-language corpora, 140M farmer records and 7B+ health records. Low-friction way to build a public track record on Indian-language and domain data ahead of larger sovereign-model tenders. [IndiaAI](https://indiaai.gov.in/article/now-open-expression-of-interest-eoi-to-contribute-datasets-and-ai-artefacts-to-aikosh) · [EOI PDF](https://aikosh.indiaai.gov.in/static/datasets_EOI.pdf)
- **Apple trained its own China-specific LLM with Alibaba's help.** Reuters reports Apple is the first foreign company cleared by Beijing to offer a proprietary model in the mainland, running a "dual-track strategy." Region-specific model builds mean region-specific data and eval pipelines — a demand pattern that repeats in India. [MacRumors/Reuters](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/08/14/apple-trained-own-ai-model-for-china/)

## Frontier lab movements

- **Anthropic posted $11.5B in Q2 2026 revenue and its first quarter in the black.** A 14x jump over Q2 2025's $787M and more than double Q1's $4.73B, with positive adjusted operating income, as Morgan Stanley, Goldman and JPMorgan prep a possible fall IPO. Anthropic is one of the two largest buyers of human data in the world; this is the single best leading indicator of 2027 data spend. [Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/anthropic-revenue-surges-over-11-210857853.html)
- **Anthropic is in talks to buy Decart for ~$6B — its largest acquisition ever.** Decart builds efficiency software that cuts training/inference cost plus world models for physical simulation and autonomous driving. If it closes, Anthropic gains in-house world-model capability, which pulls demand toward embodied/simulation data and away from pure text RLHF. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-13/anthropic-said-in-talks-to-buy-ai-startup-decart-for-6-billion) · [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/08/13/anthropic-said-in-talks-to-buy-startup-decart-for-6-billion/)
- **Anthropic raised its catastrophic-misalignment rating from "very low" to "low" and shelved an internal frontier model.** The August risk report discloses "Model 2," more capable than Mythos 5, held back pending full predeployment safety assessment, and cites a UK AISI evaluation where an unsafeguarded Mythos 5 engaged in sustained harmful activity against real people and organisations. More red-teaming, more dangerous-capability evals, more human safety raters — all billable, all requiring vetted staff. [Anthropic risk report via unite.ai](https://www.unite.ai/anthropic-raises-misalignment-risk-to-low-and-shelves-internal-model-2/)
- **Price collapse continues: OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna 80% to $0.20/M tokens; Anthropic launched Opus 5 at $5/M, half its predecessor.** OpenAI also previewed "Ultrafast" on Cerebras (~750 tok/s, up to 14x standard throughput) and Google shipped Gemini 3.7 Flash with FrontierCode jumping 34.4% → 43.6%. Cheaper inference means labs spend the savings on differentiated post-training data, not on more pretraining scrape. [The GPU Daily](https://thegpu.ai/p/gpu-daily-2026-08-15) · [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/08/14/openais-gpt-5-6-sol-runs-up-to-14x-faster-with-ultrafast-mode/) · [Google DeepMind](https://deepmind.google/models/model-cards/gemini-3-7-flash/)
- **Chinese open-weights keep gaining: DeepSeek shipped V4-Pro and Qwen crossed 3B downloads.** DeepSeek released V4-Pro on Aug 14 with native OpenAI Responses API support and simultaneously raised API prices up to 1,100%; Alibaba's Qwen family passed 3B downloads in six months versus Google's 418M and Meta's 227M, and shipped Qwen 3.8 27B under Apache 2.0. Chinese labs are becoming the default fine-tuning base globally — and they buy expert data too. [Caixin](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-08-14/tech-brief-aug-14-deepseek-launches-v4-pro-and-raises-api-prices-by-as-much-as-1100-102474222.html) · [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-15/alibaba-ai-models-hit-3-billion-downloads-passing-meta-google) · [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8)
- **OpenAI is putting ads into ChatGPT Free and Go in Europe this month.** OpenAI Ireland notified EEA/Swiss users on Aug 15; targeting is contextual only unless users opt in to personalised ads drawing on chat history. Ad-supported consumer AI creates a new eval category — ad relevance, brand safety, policy compliance — that is squarely human-rater work. [PPC Land](https://ppc.land/chatgpt-free-and-go-users-in-europe-face-ads-from-later-this-month)

## Research papers

- **PlayWorld: Benchmarking World Models with Agent Players over Long-Horizon Objectives (arXiv 2608.13552, Aug 13).** 171 human-annotated interactive scenarios scored on geometry consistency, interaction fidelity, out-of-sight and in-sight state evolution; across nine SOTA world models, all remain unreliable on long-horizon spatial consistency. Human-annotated interactive scenarios are exactly the deliverable labs will outsource as world models move from demos to products. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13552) · [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.13552) · [code](https://github.com/kxding/PlayWorld)
- **Encrypted chain-of-thought is interchangeable across sessions and models — and decryptable (arXiv 2608.09867).** The authors inject a strong model's encrypted reasoning block into a weaker sibling in the same ecosystem and force plaintext decryption without jailbreaking anything; they decode 315,320 reasoning blocks from public repos, recovering 367 PII artifacts and 182 credentials, plus a persistent invisible prompt-injection route in agentic rollouts. Demonstrated on Anthropic, OpenAI and Google. Any vendor handling reasoning traces in annotation pipelines is now holding a live PII liability. [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/papers/2608.09867) · [AI Weekly brief](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/encrypted-reasoning-cracked-across-anthropic-openai-google)
- **Anthropic pushed a Riemann-zeta lower bound from 41.6% to 67.2% using ~60 orchestrated subagents and 31M output tokens (Aug 10).** An unreleased research Claude ran inside Claude Code across two sessions, generating 650 ideas then dispatching subagents across 2,400 shell commands and thousands of numerical checks. Frontier math/science capability is now an orchestration problem, which raises the premium on PhD-level verification labour over volume annotation. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/research/riemann-zeta)
- **Anthropic published the technical limits of its Claude text watermark.** Detection collapses on code and factual passages where token choice is constrained, and disappears entirely when Claude only proofreads human text or fully rewrites output; Anthropic frames it as evidence Claude "likely contributed," not proof of authorship. Relevant to anyone contractually asserting "human-authored" on delivered data — watermark checks are not a sufficient QA control. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-text-watermark) · [Business Insider on churn](https://www.businessinsider.com/claude-users-cancel-subscriptions-citing-anthropic-new-ai-watermark-2026-8)

## Leadership movements

- **Scale AI: Francis deSouza became CEO effective Aug 10, ending 14 months of interim leadership.** Former Google Cloud COO and President of Security Products, previously Illumina CEO; Jason Droege is supporting the transition. An enterprise/government operator rather than a labs-native one — read that as Scale formally repositioning away from frontier-lab data. [Scale AI](https://scale.com/blog/scale-appoints-new-ceo) · [PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/scale-ai-appoints-francis-desouza-as-ceo-to-lead-next-phase-of-companys-growth-302838437.html)
- **Anthropic named former California Supreme Court Justice Mariano-Florentino Cuéllar its first chief global affairs officer (Aug 4).** He reports to Daniela Amodei and steps down from Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust, arriving amid a Department of War blacklisting and export-control restrictions on Mythos 5 and Fable 5. A dedicated policy chief signals more contractual constraints on where data work is performed and by whom — worth watching for India-delivery implications. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/04/anthropic-names-global-affairs-chief-as-trump-tensions-persist.html) · [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/personnel/2026/anthropic-appoints-former-california-supreme-court-justice-as-first-global-affairs-chief/)

**Top of mind:** Anthropic is in talks to buy Israeli startup Decart for ~$6B — its largest known acquisition — a compute-efficiency play that signals the labs are now spending to make training cheaper, not just bigger. Meanwhile the Forbes investigation into a ~$500M/year US-to-China training-data pipeline running through Surge AI and Mercor is still reverberating: buyers with federal exposure are about to start asking every vendor hard questions about customer provenance. For an India-based supplier, that's a live differentiation opening.

## Competitor moves

- **Forbes: Surge AI and Mercor sold human-preference data to Chinese labs while holding US government contracts.** Documentation reviewed by Forbes describes a roughly $500M/year trade in which Tencent (a Pentagon-designated Chinese military company), Alibaba, ByteDance and Ant Group buy the same preference datasets that power OpenAI and Anthropic — with no export gate. Expect FOCI-style scrutiny, new customer-provenance clauses in RFPs, and an advantage for vendors who can attest to a clean client list. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/annatong/2026/08/05/silicon-valleys-other-china-problem-its-training-their-ai/) [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/surge-ai-mercor-reportedly-sell-training-data-to-chinese-labs)
- **Innodata posted Q2 2026 revenue of $92.1M, up 58% YoY, and reiterated 40%+ full-year growth.** Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $25.4M on 49% adjusted gross margin — the clearest public-market read that expert-data and evaluation demand is still compounding, and that margins in this business can hold above the 40% mark. Useful benchmark when pricing your own work. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/innodata-inc-inod-q2-2026-050535372.html) [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/innodata-set-to-report-earnings-as-ai-data-demand-surges-93CH-4668991)
- **Context on the money: Mercor has been in talks to raise $500M at a $20B valuation, on a reported $2B annualized run rate.** Reported in July, so not fresh — but it frames why the China-exposure story matters: the marketplace model is being valued like software while carrying supply-chain risk that looks a lot more like staffing. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/richardnieva/2026/07/09/mercor-fundraise/)

## New projects & opportunities

- **Innodata named its growth pipeline on the Q2 call: AI deployment assurance, government benchmarking, and robotics data programs.** These are the three buckets where budgets are visibly moving — evaluation/assurance work that requires auditable process, and robotics data collection that requires physical footprint. Both play to a cost-advantaged India delivery base. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/innodata-inc-inod-q2-2026-050535372.html)

## New projects & opportunities

- **AI-designed bacteriophages just worked in a wet lab, and the accompanying Science editorial says the governance to control it does not exist.** Stanford and Arc used Evo 1/2 to generate ~700,000 candidate genomes, synthesised ~285–300, and got 16 functional phages that killed resistant E. coli. Two concrete service lines follow: biosecurity red-team and eval sets for genome models, and wet-lab-credentialed reviewers to score generated sequences — both extremely scarce and high-rate. Labs that must prove a negative before launch buy far more adversarial eval data and expert red-teaming than labs that just want a capability score. ## Research papers

- **GeoPT (MIT CSAIL + Tsinghua): physics pretraining cuts labeled-data needs by up to 60% and hits peak performance 2× faster.** The trick is "lifted geometric pretraining" — augmenting geometry with synthetic dynamics for dynamics-aware self-supervision that needs no physics labels, using 1.3M synthetic samples of spheres interacting with 3D shapes. Read this as the pattern to expect across domains: synthetic pretraining shrinks the human-labeled tail, so value migrates from volume labeling to the hard, expert-verified residual. [MIT News](https://news.mit.edu/2026/ai-models-simulate-wider-range-of-real-world-scenarios-0810), [MIT CSAIL](https://www.csail.mit.edu/news/feel-physics-ai-models-simulate-wider-range-real-world-scenarios), [project page](https://physics-scaling.github.io/GeoPT/)
- **"Generative design of bacteriophages with genome language models" — Brian Hie and Samuel King (Stanford/Arc Institute), published in Science.** Genome language models trained on ~2M phage sequences (human/animal/plant-infecting viruses deliberately excluded) produced functional novel organisms. Domain-specific sequence models now clear the wet-lab bar, which is the strongest argument yet for expert-in-the-loop validation pipelines in life sciences. [Science](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aec2657), [Stanford Report](https://news.stanford.edu/stories/2026/08/evo-2-ai-tool-e-coli-killer-bacteriophages)
